Subject: Capacity slate sizing — pivot proposal for QuantumWell

Ava —

Following our sync last week I put together a compact pivot that aligns to QuantumWell's Q2 launch window and procurement constraints. High level: we propose an anchored slate with a modest base floor for steady inference and a clearly defined ramp path tied to usage milestones. Key points in the attached workbook (QW_pivot_slate_v1.xlsx):

- Anchor configuration (month 0): 32 GPUs total (8 nodes x 4 gpus) running mixed 8-bit quantized weights for your primary text-generation models.
- Minimum guaranteed floor: 16 GPUs reserved to ensure predictable throughput and prioritization during your first 90 days.
- Burst / surge capacity: up to +50% via reserved warm lanes and on-demand burst to our shared pool.
- Ramp schedule: add +8 GPUs at the start of months 2 and 4 (targeting 48 GPUs by month 4) with optional +8 in month 6 if usage growth meets the agreed triggers.
- SLO expectations: aiming for 95th percentile latency under 300ms for 512-token requests with the recommended batching strategy.
- Commercial note: phased billing (base reservation + usage overage). We included a conservative burn profile to help procurement.

Asks: can you confirm whether a 16 GPU minimum floor fits procurement/finance comfort? Also would like your ops lead to share any constraints on IP/networking that would affect a VPC private deployment vs. dedicated-hosted lane.

I'll loop in infra for a technical sanity-check on prewarm and KV cache sizing.

Thanks,

Jordan / Priyom / Ava / Suresh —

Quick sizing summary and recommendations (short bullets for the customer):

- Feasibility: Yes — the anchor and ramp as proposed are valid for QuantumWell's stated model mix, provided we adopt the mixed-precision + KV caching approach below.

- Recommended base configuration (customer-facing):
  • Base reservation: 32 GPUs (8 x 4-GPU nodes) as the preferred anchor; this gives headroom for model fan-out and avoids frequent cold starts.
  • Minimum floor option (procurement-friendly): 16 GPUs reserved (4 x 4-GPU nodes) with auto-prioritization for critical routes.
  • Intermediate option: 24 GPUs (6 x 4) priced ~8% higher than 16-floor but gives better latency margin.

- Why 32 preferred: at steady-state inference with KV cache hit rates > 60% and batching (dynamic batching up to 16 tokens), utilization sits ~65-75% for 512-token workloads; smaller floors (16) will see more variability and higher tail latencies during bursts.

- Tail-latency mitigation:
  • KV cache sizing: allocate ~120GB of KV cache across the fleet for primary model (est. 2.5M tokens of active context) — this reduces reprocessing and lowers p95.
  • Batching strategy: enable continuous batching with an adaptive max latency window of 20ms to avoid token-level tail spikes.
  • Canary & warmup: recommend a 48-hour canary during ramp + one prewarm window before heavy traffic; provide 5% of monthly reserved GPU-hours as warmup credits to seed embeddings/KV caches.

- Ramp schedule we can support:
  • Month 0: start at 16 reserved (if procurement requires floor).
  • Month 1: move to 24 (add +8 GPUs) after canary verification.
  • Month 3: expand to 32 (+8) based on usage triggers.
  • Optional Month 5: expand to 40–48 if growth targets met (documented in SOW).

- Delivery considerations: private VPC is supported; burst lanes will use an authenticated peering model — minimal additional network setup (static routes + SG rules) required by Suresh. No need for dedicated HSM/KMS changes unless you opt for on-prem key control.

Next steps:
- Jordan: share these bullets with QuantumWell and attach a clean version of the infra notes.
- Priyom: parallelize pricing for the 16 / 24 / 32 floors and include the warmup-credit line-item.
